column1: # gates/gate-required-floor.tsv — THE MONOTONIC FLOOR UNDER THE GATE MANIFEST'S `required` COUNT.
# jobs/nothing-ratchets-the-manifests-required-count-so-the-denominator-is-editable-downward-2026-10-02
# (found by antagonist A on #462 at the diff door, reached independently by antagonist B at the shipped-surface
# door, so it is one of that pair's common grounds).
# THE DEFECT IT CLOSES. #461 gave the suite a manifest, so a deleted gate became a RED instead of a silence. But
# the manifest's own `required` count is the denominator, and nothing bounded it from BELOW: delete a gate, flip
# its row's state to `absent`, type any single character into field 7, and `gatemanifest.sh check` reports one
# fewer required gate and EXITS 0 — the suite runs, emits GATES GREEN, and gates/verify-log.sh says OK.
# REPRODUCED at #467 before this file existed, on a throwaway copy of the real manifest with 49 stub gates:
# removing gates/regress/21-review-brilliant.js and editing two fields of its row took the line from
# "49 required, 49 present, 0 missing" to "48 required, 48 present, 0 missing" at exit 0. That gate is the one
# CLAUDE.md names as the only cover for brilliancy explanations — the item Kunal raised five times before it
# landed. So the frozen denominator CLAUDE.md records at #405 was not merely frozen here, it was EDITABLE
# DOWNWARD, which is worse, because the push gate reads the manifest's own self-report.
# THE MECHANISM, and it is borrowed rather than invented. gates/build-numbers.tsv's discipline is append-only and
# a row is never deleted; gates/held-trees.tsv proved a committed register keyed on things a later run can
# compute with no network and no tracker. This file is the same shape with ONE addition those two do not have:
# a CHAIN FIELD. Every row carries the floor value that stood BEFORE it, so row i's `prev` must equal row i-1's
# `floor`. Deleting or editing an INTERIOR row therefore breaks the chain and is a hard failure, with no git and
# no network needed.
# WHAT THIS CANNOT DO, SAID HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. An append-only register cannot detect its own
# TRAILING TRUNCATION: delete the LAST row and what remains is a perfectly consistent chain ending one step
# earlier, so the floor falls and nothing local can object. That is not a hole I can close from inside this file
# — the anchor has to be outside it — and the anchor is git. It is the subject of
# jobs/the-gate-manifest-can-be-weakened-by-hand-and-only-git-can-object-2026-10-02, which #467 leaves open
# DELIBERATELY with its baseline question answered on the job (see that job's field answeredBy_467). Do not read
# this file as closing that one. What it does close is the two-field edit above, which needed no file deletion at
# all and was therefore much the cheaper attack.
# HOW THE CURRENT FLOOR IS COMPUTED: replay the rows in file order; the floor is the LAST row's value. A `raise`
# must increase it; a `lower` must decrease it by EXACTLY ONE, carry a reason in field 7, and name in field 8 a
# gate whose state in gate-manifest.tsv is `retired`; and the chain must be intact.
# THE "EXACTLY ONE" AND THE GATE FIELD BOTH COME FROM ANTAGONIST B's VETO ON THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FILE, and
# they are the difference between a ratchet and a one-shot release valve. As first written, `retire` lowered the
# floor to whatever the tree happened to require, so a run could delete twenty gates, hand-flip their rows to
# `absent`, retire ONE of them properly, and take the floor 49 -> 29 AT EXIT 0 - by following the instruction the
# breach message itself printed. B measured it end to end, including a verify-log.sh OK over the resulting log,
# and I reproduced it before changing anything. The register would then have carried, permanently, one row naming
# one gate and accounting for twenty: worse than the plain two-field diff #461 left behind, because it arrives
# laundered through this project's own audit anchor looking like due process.
# ONE GATE LEAVES PER ROW. So the register's row count IS the number of retirements and cannot be made to stand
# for more, and `retire` REFUSES when the tree is more than one gate below the floor, listing the others by name.
# The gate field closes the other half B found: a hand-APPENDED `lower` row, which is neither an edit nor a
# deletion and which the chain field therefore had nothing to say about. A hand-appended row must now also name a
# gate the MANIFEST records as retired, so the two files have to agree and the reason lands in the commit diff.
# AND THE REASON FIELD IS NO LONGER LENGTH-TESTED. The first version required 12 characters, which B showed wrong
# in both directions: twelve junk characters passed, while the genuine reason "slow gate" was REFUSED because the
# length was measured after spaces were stripped - and the error quoted `slowgate` back at the user. A length test
# on free text is not a check. It was replaced by the structural test above, not tuned.
# WHO WRITES IT: `gatemanifest.sh sync` raises it when it adds required rows; `gatemanifest.sh retire` lowers it
# when it retires one. BOTH REFUSE unless CT_BUILD and CT_RUNID are set (B's F4: the first version inherited
# gatemanifest.sh's `unknown` / `unknown-run` fallback and wrote it into THIS file, where a row is never deleted -
# so the documented happy path would have left a permanently unattributable row in the project's new audit
# anchor). `check` only ever COMPARES - it never writes. That separation is #454's lesson ("is it recorded" and
# "is it mine" are two questions, and conflating them deadlocked the build): a tool that writes its own floor and
# then reads it back as authority is the check and the thing being checked being the same object, which is the
# trap CLAUDE.md now records ten times.
# floor  prev  kind   at          build  runId                   why                                   gate

column7: seeded at the measured required count of the tree that introduced the floor. MEASURED by gates/gatemanifest.sh check on 8de6233: 49 required, 49 present, 0 missing, 0 unlisted, 5 known-absent. Not chosen - read off the tool.
